messages:
alex_m: Heads-up — customer reported export includes KMS ciphertext in exported JSON (they flagged it as PII).

samira: ugh, can you paste a redacted sample?

alex_m: redacted snippet pasted below:
```json
{
  "timestamp": "2026-03-20T14:02:11Z",
  "action": "model.deploy",
  "user": "redacted",
  "meta.kms_ciphertext": "BASE64_ABCD...=="
}
```

jordan_l: that's definitely the envelope ciphertext from our KMS wrapper. it should NEVER be surfaced in customer-facing audit exports.

mina_sec: this smells like the ev-log schema flattening change (ev-log v2) — we moved nested meta.* into top-level columns and the export pipeline flattens all keys. KMS metadata got pulled through.

alex_m: repro steps I used: 1) Console > Audit Viewer, 2) filter project=acme-corp, 3) Export -> JSON, 4) grep for "kms". easy to reproduce.

samira: customer also said some users with role `audit_viewer` couldn't use the CSV export but could hit JSON via API. is there an RBAC mismatch?

jordan_l: there was an RBAC policy generator change in last Thursday's roll that renamed `audit.export` -> `audit.export_view` for some roles. audit_viewer lost explicit export right and fell back to a legacy export codepath. legacy path missed the new sanitizer.

mina_sec: immediate mitigation options: 
1) quick patch in export service to redact any keys that match /kms|ciphertext|key_meta/ or base64 blobs.
2) rollback flattening in export pipeline.
3) re-grant `audit.export` to `audit_viewer` for affected tenants until sanitized export is live.

alex_m: lowest-risk is the export sanitizer patch. small surface, can canary quickly. jic we should do re-grant while canary is running.

samira: I opened SEC-4721 with repro, sample, and suggested quickfix. link: https://github.com/redwood/inference/issues/4721

jordan_l: also need customer-facing validation: when a customer requests an export we should validate event schema and reject if any value looks like a KMS ciphertext (or better, strip it). otherwise we're liable. I'll draft a short policy.

mina_sec: I'll coordinate with infra to push an emergency feature flag `sanitize_audit_exports` to all Console instances. @jordan_l can you prepare the role-binding PR to re-grant audit.export for 48h?

jordan_l: on it. PR draft: https://github.com/redwood/inference/pull/8932 (wip) — will include audit-export perm change and a migration to add the missing permission back to `audit_viewer`.

audit-bot: Incident created: INC-2026-1357 assigned to eng-security, priority=P2.

alex_m: I also ran a quick grep on logs for plaintext KMS keys — nothing found. looks like only ciphertext leaked. good.

samira: added unit test in exports_test: ensures any key name containing "kms" or values matching base64 pattern are redacted. will push after review.

mina_sec: deployment plan: patch sanitizer -> enable feature flag in canary -> monitor export metrics and errors -> re-grant audit.export to impacted roles -> roll forward sanitizer to prod -> remove feature flag and bake full fix next week.

alex_m: customer informed of interim workaround: use API export with `?sanitize=true` or wait ~1h for fix.

samira: created internal doc: docs/ops/audit-export-kms-mitigation.md with timeline and action items.

mina_sec: assigning owners: sanitizer = @samira, RBAC rollback PR = @jordan_l, infra flag = @alex_m. will follow up in SEC-4721 and update INC-2026-1357.

alex_m: thanks all — please ping me on the channel when canary is green.
